references.text: Both texts deal with a discussion about the cause of blindness and God's power to heal. In John 9, the disciples ask whether sin is the cause of blindness, just as skeptics in John 11:37 question whether Jesus could have prevented death, even though he had previously opened the eyes of a blind man.

In John 11:4, Jesus says that the sickness is not unto death but for God's glory. This stands in direct contrast to the question in verse 37, where people doubt whether Jesus could prevent death, while Jesus himself has confirmed that death is not the end in God's plan.

Martha expresses the same faith as the skeptics in verse 37, but with trust: 'If you had been here, my brother would not have died.' Both statements acknowledge Jesus' previous miracles and question his ability to intervene at the moment of death.

Mary says to Jesus: 'If you had been here, my brother would not have died.' This is a direct repetition of the logic in verse 37, where people wonder why Jesus did not prevent death, given his ability to perform other miracles.

Jesus answers the doubt in verse 37 by saying: 'If you believe, you will see the glory of God.' This connects the question about Jesus' power (to prevent death) directly to faith that he can do it, even though it seems impossible.
